children: traded lower on Friday, and rival Vera Therapeutics
gained after the U.S. FDA extended its review of the former’s kidney disease drug povetacicept, a decision Leerink Partners identified as “quite disappointing.”
Announcing the revised Feb. 28 target action date issued in connection with its Biologics License Application for povetacicept in IgA nephropathy, Vertex
on Wednesday attributed the delay to an information request
The company's stock lost more than 10% after the announcement, its worst intra-day performance since August 2025.
, whose once-weekly injectable branded as Trutakna received the U.S. accelerated approval for IgA nephropathy in July, added ~15% in reaction, recording its best intraday gain since June 2025.
Noting the review extension as “quite disappointing,” Leerink Partners analyst David Risinger, who has an Outperform rating on Vertex

, remained hopeful. “We now assume that pove will be approved within the next three months,” Risinger wrote, according to Bloomberg.“Although we cannot predict the FDA label, we are hoping that if blood monitoring is required, it is infrequent and thus does not materially impact commercial prospects,” the analyst added.
Baird analyst Brian Skorney, who has an Underperform rating on Vertex
, argued that the delay allows rivals Vera

to extend their lead in the IgAN market with their directly competitive, approved drugs. “In a worst-case scenario, the FDA request is looking closer at potential need for IgG monitoring for povetacicept,” Skorney added.

Raymond James analyst Christopher Raymond argued that the insufficient details provided on the reason for the delay are "likely to fuel bearish speculation around the drug’s safety profile.” Raymond, who has a Market Perform rating on VRTX, says he “can’t argue that this program does not now carry a meaningfully higher level of risk.”

title: Vertex falls on “disappointing” FDA delay on kidney drug review; Vera rises
